typography_notes: Entirely sans-serif (Arial/Helvetica-like). Every text line is bold. Four size tiers, all center-aligned: '[4] Introduction to' medium (~36pt equivalent), 'Deep Learning' largest (~54pt), 'and' smallest (~28pt), 'CNN' large (~48pt). No italics, no underlines, no all-caps styling (CNN is naturally an acronym). Line spacing is generous, roughly 1.5x, giving an airy stacked title. The '[4]' prefix is a lecture/chapter number rendered inline at the same size as the rest of its line.
animation_state: Static title slide; no build state visible. A presenter's mouse cursor is frozen on-screen at lower-left-of-center, indicating this is a frame from a recorded lecture video, but no elements appear mid-reveal.
recreation_brief: 1. Create a 16:9 slide with a white (#FFFFFF) background. 2. Draw a rectangle covering the slide inset ~6% from left/right and ~7% from top (extend to bottom edge); set its fill to light gray #E9E9E9 and its outline to dark red #C11B22, weight ~1.5pt, no shadow. 3. Insert a centered text box spanning ~25%-75% width, positioned from ~22% to ~80% height, with center alignment and dark red (#C11B22) bold sans-serif (Arial) text. 4. Type four paragraphs, centered, with these sizes and line breaks exactly: line 1 '[4] Introduction to' (~36pt bold), line 2 'Deep Learning' (~54pt bold), line 3 'and' (~28pt bold), line 4 'CNN' (~48pt bold); set paragraph line spacing to ~1.5. 5. Optionally add a small mouse-cursor arrow icon (white arrow, dark outline) at ~29% from left and ~84% from top to mimic the captured presenter pointer — this is optional since it is a recording artifact. 6. Do NOT add the bottom black strip; it is video letterboxing, not slide content. 7. Verify: no bullets, no images, no charts — the slide consists solely of the framed gray field and the four-line red centered title.
